version.changelog:
**Version 1.2.0 — Data Privacy & Requirements Improvements**

- Added an explicit privacy/disclosure section detailing how repository code is transmitted to model providers, with clarification on diff truncation and token use.
- Declared required environment variables and binaries in SKILL.md under a new `requires` field.
- Updated token scope recommendations for improved least-privilege security.
- Minor clarifications on data flow, privacy, and restrictions in documentation.
- No core logic or functionality changes to the review or triage flow.

llm.summary: The skill's behavior mostly matches its stated purpose (automated dual-model PR reviews) but there are mismatches between declared requirements and the actual script (notably missing the openclaw CLI in declared binaries) and privacy-sensitive actions (sending diffs to configured model providers) that the user should verify before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (dual-model PR review, auto-merge, triage) aligns with what the script does (fetch PRs, build review prompts, dispatch to agents, comment/merge). However, registry metadata lists no required binaries while SKILL.md and scripts expect gh, python3, curl — and the script also calls the openclaw CLI (openclaw agent) which is not declared in either metadata or SKILL.md's front-matter. This mismatch is coherence noise: openclaw is essential for the skill to function but is not declared.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts explicitly instruct the agent to send PR diffs and file listings to configured model providers via the OpenClaw agent. That is consistent with the stated purpose but is privacy-sensitive: repository code (diffs) will be transmitted to whatever model endpoints the OpenClaw agent is configured to use. The SKILL.md claims tokens are never passed to models and the script does not appear to include the GH_TOKEN inside the prompt payload, which is good — but you must trust the configured agent endpoints. The script also truncates diffs to 500 lines and supports dry-run and skip labels, which limits exposure.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only with a helper script) — nothing is downloaded or extracted from external URLs during install. The runtime requires existing CLI tools; this is low install risk. Still, the runtime depends on an undeclared openclaw binary and on standard tools (curl, python3, gh).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests GH_TOKEN (declared). Additional config env vars (GUARDIAN_*) are optional and proportional. The script will call gh auth token to obtain a token if GH_TOKEN is not set, which means the gh CLI may read stored credentials — the SKILL.md did not highlight that fallback behavior clearly. The SKILL.md's recommended scopes are roughly correct but somewhat confusing in wording; ensure you grant least-privilege (read-only) token if you won't use auto-merge.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable; it does not request permanent platform presence and does not attempt to modify other skills or agent-wide configuration. Actions it takes (comments, merges, labels) are standard for a repo automation tool and require GitHub API privileges which are constrained to GH_TOKEN.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing, verify these points: (1) The script requires the openclaw CLI at runtime (openclaw agent --agent ...), but that binary is not listed in registry metadata — ensure you have and trust the OpenClaw agent client and its configuration. (2) The skill will transmit PR diffs and file listings to whatever model endpoints your OpenClaw agent is configured to use — confirm those model providers and policies (don’t run this against untrusted external models if the repo is sensitive). (3) Provide a least-privilege GH token (read-only repo access if you will not use auto-merge); test with GUARDIAN_AUTO_MERGE=false and --dry-run first. (4) Review the script locally to ensure the agent targets (keats, openforge-cloud, etc.) are acceptable for your environment or editable. (5) Because the registry metadata and SKILL.md disagree about required binaries, run the script in a safe environment to confirm and fill any missing runtime dependencies. If you cannot trust the configured OpenClaw model endpoints or need to keep code private, do not enable auto-merge nor run the skill against sensitive repositories.
